title: Who Skipped Review?

narrative.intro: The library hit the front page of a link aggregator overnight and downloads 10x'd in a day. Contributors you've never heard of started opening PRs, and in the rush to keep up, some things got merged fast. Now there's a bug in production - a config default got flipped that never should have shipped. Every commit on main this week is signed. Only one has no linked change request explaining why it happened.
narrative.correctDebrief: Correct - "flip default timeout to 100ms" has no Refs: CR-NNN anywhere in it, unlike every other commit here. It's still signed - nobody's impersonating anybody, that's not the gap. Change Control isn't about identity, it's about traceability: a record of why a change happened and who actually signed off on it as a change, not just who authored the commit. That's the gap that let a bad default ship straight to main with nobody accountable for the decision.
narrative.incorrectDebrief: Check every commit message for a "Refs: CR-NNN" line, not just whether it's signed - all four of these are signed, that's not the tell. The one that broke prod is the one with no linked change request at all.
